holidays.name: National Thank You Note Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to sitting down with a pen and paper to thank everyone who gave you a gift, ideally before you forget who gave you the mysterious fondue set.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance in the United States that falls the day after Christmas, when gift-receiving is fresh and etiquette guilt is at its peak.
holidays.funFact: Etiquette experts have long advised sending thank-you notes within a couple of weeks of receiving a gift, and a handwritten note is still considered the gold standard.

holidays.name: National Candy Cane Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the peppermint-striped hook of sugar that decorates trees and sticks to coat pockets across the holiday season.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance in the United States, tied to the candy cane's role as a classic Christmas treat.
holidays.funFact: Candy canes are often said to have been created in 1670 by a choirmaster in Germany who bent sugar sticks to resemble shepherd's crooks, though historians consider the story more legend than documented fact.

holidays.name: Boxing Day
holidays.description: A public holiday in the UK, Canada, Australia, and other Commonwealth countries, where people recover from Christmas by shopping sales, watching sports, and eating leftovers. No actual boxing is required.
holidays.origin: Traditionally linked to giving boxes of money or gifts to servants, tradespeople, and the less fortunate the day after Christmas. Church alms boxes opened on St. Stephen's Day are also part of the story.
holidays.funFact: Despite the name, Boxing Day has nothing to do with the sport. It is also a huge day for football matches in England and for the start of the Sydney to Hobart yacht race in Australia.

holidays.name: Kwanzaa Begins (Umoja Day)
holidays.description: The first day of the seven-day Kwanzaa celebration, focused on Umoja, meaning unity, with the lighting of the first candle on the kinara.
holidays.origin: Created in 1966 by Dr. Maulana Karenga as a celebration of African American culture and heritage, drawing on African harvest festivals.
holidays.funFact: The name Kwanzaa comes from the Swahili phrase 'matunda ya kwanza,' meaning 'first fruits,' and the extra 'a' was added to give the word seven letters, one for each of the seven principles.

holidays.name: Festivus Aftermath: Boxing Day Leftovers Day
holidays.description: An informal day of reinventing yesterday's feast into sandwiches, casseroles, and questionable turkey-cranberry-stuffing towers.
holidays.origin: An informal tradition rooted in the practice of eating holiday meal remnants the day after Christmas.
holidays.funFact: Many families swear the best sandwich of the whole year is the next-day turkey, stuffing, and cranberry stack, which some fans say rivals the original dinner.
